items.title: Actual PBPS: detailed balance after independent reference averaging

source.attribution: Fan Chen, Sinho Chewi, Jianfeng Lu and Matthew S. Zhang. ASTIS completes the measurable-indicator, finite signed Fubini and same-actual-witness details; this is not a complete paper.
source.anchor: Proposition3.2; A.1 lines819-820 and A.2 lines832-853; standing assumptions1.1 and scale convention2.2

items.statement: Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel space. Assume V is C2, 0<alpha<=beta, alpha||v||^2<=D2V(x)[v,v]<=beta||v||^2 for every x,v, eta>0 and beta eta<=1. For each y let q_y be the normalized law proportional to exp(-V(x)-||x-y||^2/(2 eta)) dx. Draw the reference r from q_y, momentum p from the standard Gaussian and unit exponential clocks independently. Run the actual fixed-reference flow to time pi and return its position. The SAME global jointly measurable probability kernel H(y,x) given by this literal pushforward satisfies detailed balance with q_y for EVERY y. The existing raw covered-arc and fallback equations, parameterwise clock-AE interval coverage, local zero-time law and half-turn initialization outputs are retained. None of these construction, normalization, probability or integrability facts is a new hypothesis.
assumptions: Exactly the six analytic assumptions in the statement; finite real Hilbert Borel E includes dimension zero.

Literal flow: c=y-eta grad V(r); x_t=c+cos(t)(x-c)+sqrt(eta)sin(t)p, p_t=-sin(t)(x-c)/sqrt(eta)+cos(t)p. Bounce reflects in grad V(x)-grad V(r), with identity at zero normal; rate sqrt(eta)max(0,<p,grad V(x)-grad V(r)>).

Independent unit exponential thresholds, integrated-hazard hitting times and the existing raw initial-state fallback define Z. The full literal recursion and retained outputs are available in the folded proposition.

Normalization, probability, joint measurability, integrability and detailed balance are derived, not extra source binders. AE initialization/coverage is parameterwise; no common null set uniform in every parameter is asserted.
